title: Runtime feature flags and operator emergency controls are environment-only or incomplete

original_titles.title: Kill switch is environment config, not an audited feature_flags row with cache invalidation

problem: runner_enabled, ai_assessment_enabled and telemetry_enabled are environment settings. There is no audited runtime feature_flags table with cache invalidation, and /health exposes DB status rather than full readiness/metrics/alerts. Operator kill switches and status page are incomplete.
impact: Changing a feature flag can require restart/config access; operators have limited visibility into worker lag, dead jobs, queue age and incident status.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Define a small typed feature_flags table scoped to tenant/event with flag key, value, reason, actor, changed_at and expiry. Use a strict allow-list; never allow flags to grant permissions or expose GT.
Add admin + step-up control for high-risk flags, with audit and cache invalidation/short TTL. Keep production boot defaults fail-closed.
Add /readyz for dependencies and startup readiness, /metrics for safe service/queue metrics and worker heartbeat, and alert thresholds for job age/dead letters.
Publish an operator status/incident page with maintenance mode and a manual fallback if the platform is unavailable.
Test kill-switch propagation across API/worker instances and prove that disabling runner/AI does not disable submission or result access.

acceptance_criteria: Critical feature flags change without an uncontrolled restart and every change is audited.
Readiness and metrics indicate API, DB and worker health separately.
An operator can communicate an incident without exposing private event data.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
